title: Pentagon Signs Oil Deal with Venezuelan Tycoon Previously Probed for Money Laundering
snippet: A Venezuelan billionaire once targeted by U.S. federal authorities in a high-profile money laundering probe has landed a lucrative defense contract to supply oil to the Pentagon.
content:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Defense has drawn sharp scrutiny after awarding a fuel procurement deal to a Venezuelan billionaire who was previously the subject of an extensive federal money laundering investigation.

A History Under Federal Scrutiny

The business magnate was previously linked by federal law enforcement agencies to broad investigative dossiers examining illicit financial flows, bribery schemes, and the systematic embezzlement of funds from Venezuela's state-owned oil enterprise, PDVSA. Although the executive managed to navigate the probes without a public conviction in U.S. courts, federal authorities had spent years tracing offshore accounts and shell companies connected to his business empire.

Questions Over Federal Vetting Procedures

Defense Department representatives maintained that all fuel contracts strictly adhere to Federal Acquisition Regulations and standard legal compliance checks before approval. However, government ethics watchdogs and foreign policy experts expressed alarm over the contract, pointing out that awarding taxpayer dollars to individuals tied to Venezuelan kleptocracy poses both reputational risks and systemic loopholes in federal contractor background checks.
